answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a refundable stake before it can trade, like a crystal-clear deposit held in escrow. A fake identity is cheap to spawn, but funding thousands of stakes is not, so an attacker faces real cost per copy. Honest agents earn fees and keep their stake; misbehaving ones lose it. Entry stays open, like a lagoon with a narrow inlet: anyone may pass, but only one at a time, and only with collateral at the gate.
